title: Compute Decimal Representation
summary: Given a positive integer n, express it as a sum of the fewest base-10 components possible, where a base-10 component is defined as a product of a single digit from 1 to 9 and a non-negative power of 10.
statement: Given a positive integer n, express it as a sum of the fewest base-10 components possible, where a base-10 component is defined as a product of a single digit from 1 to 9 and a non-negative power of 10. Return these components in descending order.
constraints: Represent positive n as nonzero decimal place-value components.
Each component is one digit from one to nine times a power of ten.
Return the fewest components in descending place order.
hints: Read digits from least significant to most significant.
For each nonzero digit, multiply it by its current power of ten.
Omitting zero positions gives the fewest components.
Reverse the collected list to descending place order.
editorial: Reverse the collected list to descending place order.

tests.explanation: The nonzero place values are 500, 30, and 7.
Zero places are omitted, leaving 1000 and 2.
